node.name: Best Basic Frittata Recipe
node.description: More a method than a recipe, this easy frittata is a delicious way to use up all those odds and ends in the fridge.
recipeIngredient: ¾ cup thinly sliced shallots, (from 2 to 3 shallots)
¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
1¼ cup shredded cheese, (such as Cheddar or Gruyere)

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C), and set an oven rack in the middle position.
recipeInstructions.name: Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C), and set an oven rack in the middle position.

recipeInstructions.text: Heat the oil in a 10-inch (25-cm) cast iron or ovenproof nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the shallots and cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 4 minutes. Do not brown. Add the cooked vegetables and stir to combine.
recipeInstructions.name: Heat the oil in a 10-inch (25-cm) cast iron or ovenproof nonstick skillet over medium heat. Add the shallots and cook, stirring frequently, until softened, 3 to 4 minutes. Do not brown. Add the cooked vegetables and stir to combine.

recipeInstructions.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, heavy cream, salt, and pepper.
recipeInstructions.name: In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, heavy cream, salt, and pepper.

recipeInstructions.text: Add the cooked vegetable mixture and cheese to the egg mixture and stir to combine. Pour the mixture back into the pan (no need to wash it), then place it in the oven and bake until set, 20 to 23 minutes. Immediately place an oven mitt over the pan handle to remind yourself that it is hot (it's easy to forget and burn your hand, and the handle stays hot for a long time). Serve the frittata directly from the pan, or use a rubber spatula to loosen the edges and slide the frittata onto a serving platter.

review.reviewBody: Hi!  Could this be made in a 13 by 9 pan instead?

Perfect basic recipe! I’ve made many frittatas and bookmarked this page for times like today when I space out on the details of  the egg/cream ratio. I made one from your recipe today. Delicious! Thank you😊
Delicious!  I added kale, spinach, a little red onion and sausage.

This was my second time making this and oh my it’s delish!  Tonight I used all the veggies in the fridge that I needed to use up.  I diced a sweet potato, sliced vidalia onion, cut corn from a cob and sliced mushrooms….tossed them in olive oil, cumin and smoked paprika.  I roasted all together in a 425 oven (30 minutes) and then followed the recipe exactly using Gruyere cheese.  As always when I use a OUAC recipe…..this was incredible!  And incredibly EASY!  This is my go to site when I need something fabulous!  OUAC never fails to wow me!  Thank you for sharing your gift!

Jeffrey
I feel your pain when it comes to shells in the eggs.  however after a culinary class  in France - (One only) I was shown how to crack an egg properly.  Do not crack on the side of the bowl.  take the egg and whack it firmly on the counter - we have granite counters and since then I have had no issues.  
hope that helps
Roberta
Proud Canadian and Oiler fan
